a peer group of its own (shared:77, not the host's): accepted
a read-only mount is not a write
host devpts / mqueue / tmpfs / proc by super block, wherever bound: refused with super block and where the host holds it
a sub-directory of a host tmpfs: refused (same super block)
a writable ext4 mount or host shm under /dev/: refused (place exempts nothing)
tmpfs/devpts/proc/mqueue with a host path or device as mount source: refused
ext4, overlay, sysfs, cgroup2, devtmpfs, fuse, 9p, ramfs, virtiofs: refused
shared:N / master:N / propagate_from:N of a group the host holds: refused
host table unreadable or empty: not established (never a pass, never 'writable')
source / dev / optional missing, unparseable, or master:99 / shared: / unbindable: not established
one refused and one not established are two problems
the six device nodes with the canonical character-device number under a --dev root: accepted
a node on another file system with the right number: accepted (identity decides)
another device number, a regular file: refused with what was read
a node outside the list (/dev/sda, mem, kmsg, ptmx): refused as any mount
a node not under a --dev destination: not a device node of the list
a node the probe did not read: not established
the host's table read before and after the session; a super block held at either moment counts; the report keeps both
a failed reading: nothing is shown to be the sandbox's
the probe's devices section on a real shell and stat

decisions_needed: Device allowance by identity: a node on ANY file system that the probe reads as the character device 1:3 under /dev/null (under a --dev destination) is accepted — the kernel's null device, whatever file system holds it. If the owner wants the node's file system or its origin (the host's /dev) to be part of the rule too, say so; today it is not, on purpose (§4.2, §5.5).

rep.host_mounts goes into RUN.json (trimmed to at/fs/dev/optional per mount): tens of KB on a host with hundreds of mounts, and it names the host's mount points. Lead: keep, or elide from RUN.json and keep it in the measurement's own evidence.

Register the kill files (tests/v2/test_v21_r3_conf_policy.py, tests/v2/test_v21_r3_conf_locale.py, and tests/v2/v21_r3_conf_rows.py is an import of the edited existing ones) and the new names _owned, _writes, _host_mounts, _device_roots, PSEUDO, DEVICES, LOCALE, _DEV, _PEER as targets; the existing kill files' order matters (first kill is attributed to the first file that kills).

If a wrapper that emits --mqueue (or --dev-bind) is ever added, confine.targets() must name it, or the judgement reports 'mounted beyond what the wrapper names' for it (the real-guest mqueue-sandbox record shows exactly that today).
not_established: A translated message of unshare/cat/sh under a non-C locale: the guest has only C, C.utf8, POSIX; nothing translated was observed. Needs an image with a non-English locale and its util-linux catalogue under the sandbox's /usr, the unshare --user true probe run under it and under C.

A super block of ANOTHER mount namespace than the controller's (another session's tmpfs reached through /proc/<pid>/root in a --bind) is not the host's and is not excluded by observation; confine.wrap binds only the workspace read-write so no command line it builds does that. No rule added (a rule 'destination also bound from the host' falsely refuses the covered --tmpfs /tmp row of read_only: ["/tmp"]).
Bare-metal Linux, a systemd host, a devtmpfs /dev, CI Linux, Windows, macOS (no backend): not run. The shared mount tree was imitated in a namespace of the container (rshared), not a systemd host.

The lifecycle claim rests on kernel behaviour that was not itself measured: a tmpfs / devpts / proc / mqueue super block lives with the mount namespace (proc's and mqueue's with the PID / IPC namespace). Measured proxies: the host's table is the same after every session; setsid_survivors is empty. A host process holding /proc/<pid>/ns/mnt of the session would keep the namespace: not looked for.
Two mounts at one path are judged by what the probe sees at the path (a covered mount is not separately observable).

Mount options other than ro/rw are recorded and decide nothing (nosuid/nodev/noexec limit execution, not what a write reaches); a super block that says ro is deliberately not credited when the mount says rw.
A confined `aisef run` end to end (no provider, no opencode) was not run.
